title: I'm building a workflow that lets AI generate Blueprint graphs inside Unreal
author: SoloGrooveGames
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with exposing Unreal projects to AI agents.

Currently it's capable of generating blueprint graphs, creating data assets, spawning actors in the level, configuring world settings etc.

In this clip, the agent generates blueprint graphs, creates data assets, spawns actors into the level, and configures world settings to create a basic FPS project from scratch.

comments.author: Otherwise_Wave9374
comments.body: Seeing the agent actually configure world settings and spawn actors makes this feel way beyond "copilot" and into real automation. What are you using for feedback, does it run a quick play-in-editor smoke test after each change, or is it mostly static validation? If you are thinking about eval harnesses for agents, I have a few lightweight ideas collected here: https://www.agentixlabs.com/blog/

comments.author: DreamNotDeferred
comments.body: I don't know if you know Ludus AI already has this. Not my product, but I have a subscription. I don't use the BP generation, I use it to teach me BP for game dev. Just FYI.

replies.author: SoloGrooveGames
replies.body: Sure, I tested all the already available solutions including Ludus, it lacked many features/details that I needed, I plan to use this on actual big projects in the future.

comments.author: MadwolfStudio
comments.body: Usage must be beyond anything imaginable, there is no way this is viable.

replies.author: SoloGrooveGames
replies.body: It's not bad, why would be? Only the relevant data is expected from a node: title, inputs/outputs and their values, connections. Pure code also has to contain this data as well.

comments.author: Char_Zulu
comments.body: I want to test this product, where can I learn more?

replies.author: SoloGrooveGames
replies.body: This also looks nice, will take a look! Took a quick look at the code, seemingly this also lacks some extra detail that is needed for actual development, but very comprehensive nevertheless!

comments.author: alphapussycat
comments.body: Only free open source is something I care about, and local LLMs should be able to use it. Otherwise the costs are too high.

replies.author: SoloGrooveGames
replies.body: It's essentially an MCP tool so all kind of LLMs can use it.

comments.author: No-Structure897
comments.body:
I been working in my plugin for this for a while,  as a recommendation:  
having specific methods to spawn stuff is not the right way to go, it might help for a demo but is better if you rely more in unreal reflection system. Also you seem to be a bit stuck between approaches, you are having c++ but apply python scripts but not taking the biggest advantages of neither. you can let python run wild and let the LLM do wtv, which si super powerful but risky  or go c++ for full control.  
I wrote adpaper about it if you are interested.  
[https://medium.com/@agenticlink/architecting-state-safe-ai-bridges-for-game-engines-4bd7cbd438cf](https://medium.com/@agenticlink/architecting-state-safe-ai-bridges-for-game-engines-4bd7cbd438cf)

comments.author: Coretahner

replies.author: Coretahner
replies.body: Lol. Though I didn't do it. Codex did it 😂

comments.author: Silly_Newt4788
comments.body: How many agents are we talking about here? I think the question eventually for AI in game dev will not be "Can AI handle code?", it will be "Can it orchestrate well enough to reduce technical debt?"
